title: Honest Causal-Slope Intervals in Sparse Instrumental Variables with a Single Direct Effect
banked_reason: D0.5 math PASS; cold tier incremental below field, paper_score_ceiling 6.4 < 7.4, salvageable=false; independent validity check confirms no bounded in-scope repair.
gap_reasons: The characterization covers one fixed dimension–sparsity–relevance sequence with at most one direct effect, leaving its broader statistical reach unestablished.

The loading-correction architecture has a substantial [BFZ antecedent](https://arxiv.org/html/1802.09117v3), so the distinct contribution is the coupled structural diameter argument and its attaining construction.

That construction enumerates dense grids and returns the full interval below an astronomical public threshold, supplying neither a usable inference diagnostic nor practical tuning for the advertised software audience.

[D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.4 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a finite-data interval with uniform 90% coverage and matching eventual n^-1/4 honest-length bounds from the full fixed structural class, including dense nuisance loadings, unknown covariance, and one direct effect. The mathematical referee passed after independent PR adjudication and BFZ source attestation, but the cold novelty referee found incremental tier with score ceiling 6.4 below the 7.4 field gate. No Lean formalization was attempted; the final positioning and two ballast findings remain recorded because they cannot change the tier.
tldr: On the full Gaussian structural class with \(p=n^4\), \(s=\lfloor n^{2/3}\rfloor\), and \(h=\min\{1/4,n^{-1/4}\}\), a finite bounded instrument learner has simultaneous population loading and coordinate guarantees. Joint structural-residual inversion then gives uniformly honest connected causal-slope intervals of deterministic eventual length \(C/(\sqrt n\,h)\), despite arbitrarily dense treatment loadings, an unknown single direct-effect support, and unknown covariance matrices inside their spectral envelopes. The rational certified wrapper accepts this constructed learner, while the proved complete-record converse gives the matching lower scale. The contribution concerns this fixed experiment and an attaining finite construction; it makes no computational efficiency claim.
gap: BFZ provides projected inference for dense Gaussian regressions, while Ma and SNIV provide identification-robust coverage. These results do not by direct substitution establish the stated full-class causal-slope diameter. Separate BFZ coordinate radii divided by \(h\) retain the larger term \(s\log(p)/(nh)\).
fill: The project resolves the exact-class honest-length question through a simultaneous loading and coordinate certificate, supportwise moment projection, and a full-record converse. Its consumer is the partially linear IV workflow of ddml, for which inference feasibility need not coincide with reduced-form prediction feasibility.
